summary.headline: Pearl Global Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24.5% YoY to INR1,528 crore, with adjusted EBITDA margin at 10.7% (up 140 bps) and PAT of INR99 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR1,528 crore grew 24.5% YoY, the highest ever Q1, driven by volume growth (20.8 million pieces vs 17.2 million). Adjusted EBITDA excluding ESOP was INR164 crore (up 44.1%), margin 10.7%, and PAT INR99 crore (up 51.4%). Standalone (India) EBITDA margin fell to 6.6% from 7.3% because of Haryana wage revisions. Management reiterated double-digit full-year EBITDA margin and said FY28 INR6,000 crore revenue target could be reached earlier.

financial_highlights.metric: Dividend received from Pearl Global Hong Kong

segments.name: Bangladesh
segments.commentary: Largest geography at about 45%+ of group volume; business growing with existing and new customers. Capacity expansion of 6-7 million pieces expected operational in H2 FY27.

segments.name: Vietnam
segments.commentary: About 27% of group volume; key for high-value and outerwear products; management evaluating further capacity expansion and land acquisition completed.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: About 22% of group volume. Utilisation 65-70% on capacity basis, efficiency about 50-58%. Standalone EBITDA margin 6.6% due to Haryana wage hikes; Bihar second shed to add run-rate revenue of INR1,700-1,800 crore at full utilisation.

segments.name: Indonesia
segments.commentary: Healthy momentum off a lower base with focus on premium clients; described as not fully utilised; management expects both top line and bottom line growth.

segments.name: Guatemala
segments.commentary: Operating strategy reworked; management confident of break-even in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY28 revenue target of INR6,000 crore could be achieved earlier than planned if current trend holds; management says it may be exceeded.
Revenue CAGR range of 12-14% now seen as conservative; management indicated FY27 high-teens growth looks feasible at current run rate, subject to H2 US conditions.
Double-digit EBITDA margin expected for full FY27 and Q1 margin of about 10.7% expected to be sustained in subsequent Q1s; long-term aim 10-12% by FY28 and 11-12% as levers converge.
Installed capacity to reach about 108 million pieces after Bangladesh expansion (Sept-Oct 2026); target of 125-130 million pieces by 2028 retained, with interim capacity via partner factories.
Finance cost guided at 1.7%-1.8% of sales for FY27.
Capex of approximately INR200-250 crore planned for FY27 across geographies; detailed plan to follow in coming months.
capex_capacity: Bangladesh: capacity expansion of 6-7 million pieces plus eco-friendly laundry unit starting September, operational for orders in H2 FY27.

India: Bihar two sheds of 450 machines each; first shed (woven) operational at about 120,000-130,000 pieces per month; knit shed production expected Oct-Nov 2026; full capacity 4-5 lakh pieces per month once ramped.
India second shed revenue run-rate potential INR1,700-1,800 crore at full utilisation, expected ready Sept-Oct.
Vietnam: land acquisition completed; greenfield project planned later, with partner-factory capacity also being added.
Overseas utilisation about 75-80% on quarterly available capacity; India utilisation about 65-70%.
demand_pricing: US consumer behaviour described as healthy despite inflation; similar trends in EU and UK; retailers expected to pass on IEEPA refunds, which may support order books.
Realization uplift of INR20 per piece YoY attributed mainly to product mix (outerwear shipped in Q1); management says it is not a sustainable benchmark versus full-year average of INR643 in FY26.
Last year India had double-digit discounts tied to tariffs; management expects these to fade, supporting realization in Q2-Q4.
Retailers are ordering short-term rather than long-term; no shift to early ordering seen.
Japan: China share of clothing imports fell from about 65% to about 50%; Vietnam at 17.4%, Bangladesh at 4.3%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a one-off in Q1 revenue and any revision to full-year guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the growth is not one-off; the end of tariff overhang lifted customer orders. Full-year FY28 INR6,000 crore target now seen as achievable earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10.7% margin free of tariff impact and is standalone margin recovery possible?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there is no tariff impact in Q1 and the margin is operational. Standalone margin would be about 9%+ excluding the Haryana wage impact; target is high single-digit to double-digit in India.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 51% while gross margin rose to 51.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed this to a mix of outsourced/partner-factory production booked under other expenses and higher-value overseas products improving gross profit; management said the gross margin is sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost fall and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Net working capital days stable at about 43-44; more internal cash used instead of some receivable financing. Finance cost guided to 1.7-1.8% of sales for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are India utilisation and efficiency levels?
qa_highlights.answer: India capacity utilisation about 65-70% and efficiency about 58%; Bihar ramping up line by line; India volume up about 27% YoY.

risks_watch: Standalone India EBITDA margin compression (6.6%) from Haryana minimum wage hike of 38% and Noida hike of 21%; labour availability issues in Q1.
US tariff regime: MFN plus 10% additional tariff on India, Bangladesh, Indonesia and 12.5% on Vietnam after Section 122 expired on July 24; potential 301 tariff changes.
Freight and shipping disruption (container shortages, Bab-el-Mandeb, Strait of Hormuz energy volatility); customers currently bear freight under FOB terms.
Dependence on H2 US demand, with management flagging possible Fed rate hikes and war-related uncertainty.
Guatemala break-even targeted in FY27; Bangladesh expansion ramp-up timelines; Q2-Q4 realization trend relative to Q1 seasonality.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, FTAs and capacity; more cautious on macro, US demand in H2 and the India margin drag. Some answers were loose on specifics (capacity, utilisation), with several figures deferred to later communication.
